COMFORT_VIEW_NEW_LOOK_ONLY: Comfort view applies to the new look
THEME_HIGH_CONTRAST_NOTE: High contrast is on, so Windows sets the colors
NEW_LOOK_TOOLTIP: Turn off to compare the redesign with the original XMAT look
WHATS_NEW_SUBHEADING: The changes in the new look
WHATS_NEW_NEW_LOOK_BODY: XMAT has a new look: calmer colors, clearer text and more room for your captures. Everything works as it did before. Turn the New look switch off at any time to compare with the original.
WHATS_NEW_NEW_LOOK_WHERE: the New look switch, at the right of the menu bar
WHATS_NEW_NEW_LOOK_IMAGE: The capture view in the new look
WHATS_NEW_COLORS_BODY: Every color comes from one palette built from the Windows and Xbox colors, in a Light and a Dark theme. Status colors mean the same thing everywhere: green for 2xx, blue for 3xx, amber for 4xx and red for 5xx responses.
WHATS_NEW_COLORS_IMAGE: The capture view in the Light and Dark themes
WHATS_NEW_TABS_BODY: Capture tabs stay on one row, and tabs that don't fit move into the More menu at the end of it. Drag a tab to put it somewhere else, or move it with Ctrl+Shift+Page Up and Ctrl+Shift+Page Down.
WHATS_NEW_TABS_WHERE: the capture tabs at the top of the window
WHATS_NEW_TABS_IMAGE: Capture tabs on one row, with the More menu for the tabs that don't fit
WHATS_NEW_RESIZING_BODY: Layouts adjust as the window gets narrower. Filters move into a Filters menu, headers wrap onto a second line, and the traffic overview drops detail before anything is cut off.
WHATS_NEW_RESIZING_WHERE: resize the window, or put it beside another one
WHATS_NEW_RESIZING_IMAGE: The capture view in a narrow window
WHATS_NEW_OVERVIEW_BODY: A strip above the traffic table sums up the capture: the number of requests, requests per second, each status's share and the busiest hosts. Select a status or a host to filter the table by it.
WHATS_NEW_OVERVIEW_IMAGE: The traffic overview, with the requests, their statuses and the busiest hosts
WHATS_NEW_COLUMN_SUMMARIES_BODY: Every column in the traffic table has an info icon. Select it for a histogram of the column's most common values, with counts and percentages, then select a value to filter the table by it.
WHATS_NEW_COLUMN_SUMMARIES_WHERE: the info icon in a column header
WHATS_NEW_COLUMN_SUMMARIES_IMAGE: The Host column's summary: the most common hosts, with their counts and percentages
WHATS_NEW_VOLUME_BODY: The timeline can show volume: the number of requests in each second of the capture. Select a moment in it to select that second's first request in the traffic table.
WHATS_NEW_VOLUME_IMAGE: The timeline showing the number of requests in each second
WHATS_NEW_COMFORT_VIEW_BODY: Comfort view, on at first, gives rows and controls more room. Turn it off for a compact layout that fits more requests on the screen.
WHATS_NEW_COMFORT_VIEW_IMAGE: The traffic table with Comfort view on, and off
WHATS_NEW_CONTEXT_MENUS_BODY: Right-click menus put their commands in groups under labels, with more room between items and a width that suits their text.
WHATS_NEW_CONTEXT_MENUS_WHERE: right-click a request in the traffic table
WHATS_NEW_CONTEXT_MENUS_IMAGE: A request's context menu, with its commands in labeled groups
WHATS_NEW_ACCESSIBILITY_BODY: Text meets WCAG contrast in both themes, and XMAT follows Windows contrast themes. Counts and charts say what they show in words, not by color alone, and the new controls work from the keyboard with a visible focus.
WHATS_NEW_ACCESSIBILITY_IMAGE: The capture view in a Windows contrast theme

SANITIZED_EXPORT_CONFIRM:
The sanitized SAZ removes recognized credentials, cookies, keys, tokens and personal identifiers from headers, URLs and supported bodies. Client IP metadata, process information and raw request paths are left out.

JSON, XML, form and plain-text bodies are inspected, including supported compression. Binary, unsupported, malformed or oversized bodies are omitted. Native XMATCAP saves and ordinary exports remain unsanitized.

Automatic scanning cannot recognize all secrets or personal identifiers. Review the exported archive before sharing it. Continue?

HOST_LISTS_WINDOW_INTRO: These Block and Bypass lists are shared by every capture in this session; any change, including Clear All, applies to new requests and connections in every capture immediately. Block stops matching requests and wins when a host is in both lists. The lists are cleared when XMAT exits.
HOST_LISTS_SCOPE: These lists are shared by every capture in this session, so changes here, including Clear All, apply to every capture. They are not saved when XMAT exits.
HOST_LIST_PATTERN_HELP: A host entry applies to every port and does not include subdomains, so do not add a port (such as example.com:443). In a pattern that contains * or a path, text such as :8080 is matched literally and is not a port filter. Write IPv6 addresses in patterns without brackets, such as 2001:db8::* or ::1/api/*; an IPv6 pattern with brackets never matches.
HOST_LIST_BYPASS_TIMING: Bypass skips HTTPS decryption for new connections only; connections that are already open keep their current mode. This is not the Windows proxy bypass list.
HOST_LIST_PORT_NOT_ALLOWED: "{0}" includes a port. Host list entries apply to every port, so enter the host without the port.
HOST_LIST_ADD_BYPASS: Add "{0}" to Bypass List (HTTPS decryption bypass, new connections only)
HOST_LIST_REMOVE_BYPASS: Remove "{0}" from Bypass List (new connections only)
HOST_LIST_BLOCK_WINS: Block wins for new connections; bypassed connections that are already open continue until they close.
HOST_LIST_NO_HOST: No host is available for this item
HOST_LIST_NO_PHYSICAL_HOST: No single captured host for this endpoint (synthesized, combined or older data)
MENU_BYPASS_DESCRIPTION: Skips HTTPS decryption for new connections
MENU_REMOVE_BYPASS_DESCRIPTION: Decrypts HTTPS again for new connections
HOST_LISTS_WINDOW_LEAD: These Block and Bypass lists are shared by every capture in this session.
HOST_LISTS_WINDOW_FACT_CHANGES: Changes, including Clear all, apply right away to new requests and connections in every capture.
HOST_LISTS_WINDOW_FACT_BLOCK: Block stops matching requests, and it wins when a host is in both lists.
HOST_LISTS_WINDOW_FACT_EXIT: The lists are cleared when XMAT exits.
HOST_LIST_BLOCK_EXAMPLE_ADDRESSES: Every IP address that starts with 192.168.1.
HOST_LIST_RULE_HOST: A host entry matches that host on every port, but not its subdomains.
HOST_LIST_RULE_PORT: Leave the port out: `example.com:443` is not accepted.
HOST_LIST_RULE_PATTERN: An entry with `*` or a path is a pattern, and `*` matches any text.
HOST_LIST_RULE_LITERAL: In a pattern, text such as `:8080` is matched literally, not as a port.
HOST_LIST_RULE_IPV6: Write IPv6 addresses in patterns without brackets, such as `2001:db8::*` or `::1/api/*`. An IPv6 pattern with brackets never matches.
HOST_LIST_BLOCK_DESCRIPTION: Requests to these hosts are blocked in every capture this session. The list clears when XMAT exits.
HOST_LIST_BLOCK_SUMMARY: Requests to these hosts are blocked in every capture this session.
HOST_LIST_BYPASS_DESCRIPTION: HTTPS traffic to these hosts passes through XMAT without decryption in every capture this session. Changes apply to new connections. The list clears when XMAT exits.
HOST_LIST_BYPASS_SUMMARY: HTTPS traffic to these hosts passes through XMAT without decryption in every capture this session.
TIMELINE_AUTOMATION_HELP: Shows each request as a bar over time, colored by its response status. The connections list shows the same requests and works with the keyboard.
